title: G3 under a late GNSS bias
statement: The guarded M9.1 controller touches down within R1 (vertical speed at most 3 m/s) when the GNSS position is biased by 5 to 30 m, whenever the bias starts within the first 20 s of the flight.
origin: Derived from M9.1 criterion G3 (docs/m9-powered-landing.md), registered and supported only with the bias present from 0 s: R1 met in at least 27 of 30 runs. This claim extends the onset to 0-20 s as a separate, new hypothesis; it does not change G3. M14 (docs/m14-evidence-robustness.md) reported that onsets of 2, 5 and 10 s at 5 and 10 m fail.

assumptions.description: Instant the GNSS bias starts. Registered at 0 s.
assumptions.name: onset_s

assumptions.description: GNSS position bias in x and z. Registered as uniform draws over [5, 30] m; the base case uses 15 m.
assumptions.name: magnitude_m

rules.intervention: predicted result in at least role_threshold of the seeds and exact McNemar p below alpha in the predicted direction
rules.refutation: lower Clopper-Pearson 95 % bound of the violation rate at the counterexample above the claim tolerance, with byte reproduction

counterexample.description: The minimised counterexample on its discovery seed.

mitigation-threshold-1m.description: The counterexample with the mitigation Altimeter rejection threshold 1 m.

mitigation-threshold-2m.description: The counterexample with the mitigation Altimeter rejection threshold 2 m.

registered.description: The registered conditions on the same seed.

twin.description: Counterfactual twin: the counterexample with onset_s at its registered value.

mechanism.statement: After a late onset the altimeter residual stays under the 3 m rejection threshold, so the altimeter is never rejected and rule 1 of guarded never engages; with rule 1 engaged, the bias no longer matters. With the bias from 0 s, the estimator starts on the biased GNSS fix, the residual exceeds the threshold at once and rule 1 protects the landing.

interventions.description: Lower the rejection threshold to 1 m, under the residual the counterexample shows, so that rule 1 can engage.
Make rejection impossible (threshold 1000 m) at the registered conditions, where G3 holds: if rule 1 is what protects G3, R1 now fails.

trace_checks.description: The estimator never rejects the altimeter in the counterexample runs.
Altimeter residual (reported minus believed nozzle height, with the true lever arm) stays under 3 m in the counterexample runs.
At the registered conditions the residual reaches at least 3 m.

mechanism.statement: Rival: the failure needs the corrupted velocity belief that the altimeter velocity correction creates. Without that correction it disappears even when the altimeter can never be rejected.

interventions.description: Altimeter velocity gain 0 and rejection impossible (threshold 1000 m).

mechanism.statement: Rival: the failure needs the altimeter to be blended into the estimate. Without any altimeter correction it disappears even when the altimeter can never be rejected.

interventions.description: Altimeter position and velocity gains 0 and rejection impossible (threshold 1000 m): the estimator follows the biased GNSS alone.

mitigations.title: Altimeter rejection threshold 1 m
mitigations.rationale: If masking is the mechanism, a threshold below the blended residual makes the estimator reject the altimeter after a late onset as it does after an onset at 0 s, which lets rule 1 act.

families.title: Small net GNSS bias (below the 5 m floor)

mitigations.title: Altimeter rejection threshold 2 m
mitigations.rationale: A smaller change of the same gain, to see whether the trade-off depends on how far the threshold moves.

families.title: Small net GNSS bias (below the 5 m floor)

open_risks: The property is violated or untested in 75 of 256 envelope cells; the claim can hold at most on the rest, at this resolution and with 4 seeds per cell.
With mitigation threshold-1m, requirement:R1_vertical_speed is still violated in 60 of 60 runs of family gnss-bias-low.
Family gnss-bias-low already violates something in at least 90 % of its runs without mitigation threshold-1m; it can show a regression only as a new violation name.
With mitigation threshold-1m, requirement:R1_vertical_speed is still violated in 60 of 60 runs of family altimeter-bias-low.
Family altimeter-bias-low already violates something in at least 90 % of its runs without mitigation threshold-1m; it can show a regression only as a new violation name.
With mitigation threshold-1m, requirement:R1_vertical_speed is still violated in 18 of 60 runs of family small-net-gnss-bias.
With mitigation threshold-2m, requirement:R1_vertical_speed is still violated in 60 of 60 runs of family gnss-bias-low.
Family gnss-bias-low already violates something in at least 90 % of its runs without mitigation threshold-2m; it can show a regression only as a new violation name.
With mitigation threshold-2m, requirement:R1_vertical_speed is still violated in 60 of 60 runs of family altimeter-bias-low.
Family altimeter-bias-low already violates something in at least 90 % of its runs without mitigation threshold-2m; it can show a regression only as a new violation name.
With mitigation threshold-2m, requirement:R1_vertical_speed is still violated in 25 of 60 runs of family small-net-gnss-bias.
The challenge also found 3 failure classes without the claim property; they are listed, not investigated.
Exploratory simulation evidence on development seeds. It is not a confirmation and says nothing about a real vehicle.
